title: House-sitting scope, keys and security checks
audience: Pet and house sitters who stay in or visit a client's home to care for animals, and who hold keys and security codes
referencesAtStart: Official sources: Agriculture Victoria, Boarding establishments (updated 27 October 2025); Agriculture Victoria, Code of Practice for the Operation of Boarding Establishments (revision 1, updated October 2004; printed April 2025), boarding establishments only; City of Stonnington, Apply for a domestic animal business permit (no date shown); NSW Department of Primary Industries, NSW Animal Welfare Code of Practice No 5: dogs and cats in animal boarding establishments (no date shown); ACT Government, Registered pet businesses (no date shown); City of Burnside, Registration of a Business Involving Dogs (no date shown on page); City of South Perth, Kennel Establishment Licence (no date shown on page); Agriculture Victoria, Domestic animal businesses (list of business types) (no date shown).
learningOutcomes: Explain the difference between house sitting in the owner's home and boarding at the sitter's or another property, using the Victorian definition
Check the house, its security and its hazards before the first night, and record the check
Hold keys and codes under a written register.

instruction.heading: Boarding is defined by where the animal stays
instruction.body: Whether a pet arrangement is boarding or house sitting turns on where the animal is cared for. The Victorian boarding code describes boarding as holding one dog or cat for payment at a site other than where it normally lives (section 2.1). The Agriculture Victoria boarding establishments page (updated 27 October 2025) says every boarding establishment must be registered with the council for its area as a domestic animal business. The same page says home boarding is limited to up to two animals from one household at any one time, and section 10 of the code applies that two-animal limit. On that definition, an animal that stays in its own home is not boarded at a property other than its normal place of residence. Pet sitting in the sitter's own home may be home boarding. The Agriculture Victoria list of business types does not name house sitting. Stonnington's permit page (no date shown) lists for-profit homecare boarding among the businesses that need a permit, but does not define homecare boarding, which is council-specific.

instruction.heading: Boarding rules in other states: what is confirmed and what is not
instruction.body: New South Wales Code of Practice No 5 covers dogs and cats in boarding businesses. It requires every animal to be inspected once a day as a minimum, requires vaccination records dated no more than 12 months before admission, sets record-keeping duties, and names no licence. In the ACT, the pet business licensing scheme in Part 3A of the Animal Welfare Act 1992 reaches businesses that board animals, and a licence can run for up to five years. The ACT page treats boarding as covering both daytime and overnight care. In South Australia, the City of Burnside allows a business that runs a kennel for breeding, boarding or training dogs to apply for registration, and development approval is needed first. In Western Australia, the City of South Perth states that a licence is required to run a kennel, or to keep more dogs than the council's no-licence limit, and the council sets that limit. The page does not say whether a licence covers house sitting.

instruction.heading: Keys, security and the house check
instruction.body: A house sitter holds the client's keys, codes, alarm details and sometimes the car. Record each key and code in a register with the date received, the holder and the date returned, and store the register in a locked place. Never copy a key, and never give a code to another person. Before the first night, walk through the home and check each entry point, the alarm, the gate, the pet door and any hazards such as a pool, a stair gate, a loose fence or a toxic plant. Record the check, and tell the client what you found. If the home is unsafe or the alarm does not work, do not stay in it. Contact the client and the business's escalation contact in {{business:safety.escalation_contact}}, and record the decision. Access and alarm instructions are held in {{business:customers.access_instructions}}. Client information is covered by the privacy approach in “Privacy, security and customer property”.

procedure: Confirm where the animal will be cared for, and record whether the arrangement is in the owner's home or at another property
Check the council and state position for the arrangement and record the source and date, recording any point you cannot source.
Complete a house check before the first night, covering entry points, alarm, gate, pet door and hazards
Record each key and code in the register with the date received, the holder and the date returned
Tell the client about any hazard or fault found during the house check, and record the response
Do not stay in a home that is unsafe, and contact the escalation contact before leaving

workedExamples.situation: A sitter is asked to stay in a client's home in Victoria to care for two dogs for a week, while the client is overseas. The sitter will also take a third dog from another client to the sitter's own home on the same week.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Which parts of the arrangement might be boarding, and what must be checked?
workedExamples.reasoning: The third dog, taken to the sitter's own home, is a different arrangement. Under the Victorian home boarding rule, home boarding is limited to two animals from one household, and the dog from another client is a second household. The sitter should not take the third dog to the sitter's home until the council and Agriculture Victoria have confirmed the position in writing.

workedExamples.situation: On the first night, a sitter finds the back gate latch broken and the alarm panel showing a fault. The client's dog is in the yard.
workedExamples.reasoning: The house check has found two faults that affect the safety of the dog and the security of the home. The sitter should keep the dog inside, secure the gate as far as possible, call the client and the escalation contact, and record the faults and the response. If the home cannot be made secure, the sitter should not stay alone with the animal until the client or the escalation contact confirms the arrangement.

equipmentAndPpe: Key and code register, locked storage
House check form with entry points, alarm, gate, pet door and hazards
Phone with signal and the client and escalation contacts

commonErrors.error: Assuming all pet sitting is boarding, or that none of it is.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the place where the animal is cared for and the council position for that place.

commonErrors.error: Taking a second household's animal to the sitter's own home without a confirmed position.
commonErrors.prevention: Stop and confirm the position with the council and Agriculture Victoria before taking the animal.

commonErrors.error: Giving a key or code to a friend to help with the visits.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep keys and codes with the registered holder only, and record every change.

commonErrors.error: Skipping the house check because the client says the home is safe.
commonErrors.prevention: Complete the house check before the first night and record it.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: The boarding code's definition of boarding (care for a dog or cat for fee or reward at a property other than the animal's normal place of residence) is confirmed for boarding establishments.
A confirmation from Agriculture Victoria is needed before the business relies on any position.
In the ACT, the Part 3A pet business licence scheme reaches businesses that board animals.
The City of Burnside (SA) and the City of South Perth (WA) each set a council-specific registration or licence for kennels.
Completing this lesson does not register the business, grant a boarding licence or authorise any boarding arrangement.

qualityStandard: Every arrangement records where the animal is cared for and the council position checked for that place
Every house check is completed and recorded before the first night
Every key and code is recorded in the register, with the holder and return date
No second household's animal is taken to the sitter's home without a confirmed position
documentationEvidence: Arrangement record stating where the animal is cared for and the position checked, with source and date
House check record, with the faults and the response
Key and code register with holder, date received and date returned
Confirmation from the council or Agriculture Victoria, where obtained
summary: Boarding is defined by where the animal is cared for; Victoria's home-boarding limit is two animals from one household
Check the house before the first night, and register every key and code
Completing this lesson does not register the business or grant a boarding licence
referencesAtEnd: Official sources, as listed at the start of this lesson. Council rules apply only in the named council.

knowledgeChecks.question: Under Victoria's definition in this course, what does boarding mean?
options: Caring for any animal in any place, paid or unpaid, for as long as the owner needs the help during the week
Caring for an animal only in a licensed kennel, with the owner's written consent on file for each stay
Caring for a dog or cat for fee or reward at a property other than the animal's normal place of residence

knowledgeChecks.question: The house check finds a broken back gate latch and a dog in the yard. What is the correct action?
options: Leave the dog in the yard and fix the latch later, since the dog is safe enough outside for now at the house
Keep the dog inside, secure the gate as far as possible, call the client and escalation contact, and record the faults
Ignore the latch since the client did not mention it, and the dog seems to be settled outside for the day

knowledgeChecks.question: Where does the lesson say the key and code register must be stored?
options: In an open folder in the hall
On the sitter's personal phone only
